## Schema’s biggest lesson is what it did not do JSON-LD schema has become one of the easiest things to blame, or to celebrate, whenever AI search visibility shifts\. Ahrefs’ latest test cuts through that habit fast: adding schema alone barely changed AI citations\. The result is less a victory lap for markup than a warning about the causation trap that keeps misleading marketers\. AI-generated illustration The lure is obvious\. Ahrefs found that pages cited by AI were almost three times more likely to have JSON-LD than pages that were not cited\. That kind of gap can look like a simple optimization play, until you test the tactic directly\. Once Ahrefs tracked 1,885 pages that added JSON-LD schema and compared them with 4,000 control pages across Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and ChatGPT, the supposed advantage mostly vanished\. ## Why the correlation looked so persuasive A lot of teams want schema to be the missing switch for AI visibility because it feels concrete, controllable, and tidy\. After more than 200 hours with it, the picture that emerges is not of an assistant that replaces marketers, but of one that takes over the repetitive work that used to eat analyst time, content-team time, and a surprising amount of attention\. That matters because the product is being framed around execution, not just generation\. Agent A is built on Ahrefs’ 170T\+ indexed pages, has unrestricted access to Ahrefs data, and is meant to connect directly to the tools marketing teams already live in\. # Ahrefs launches AI agent workspace Letaido for marketers and agencies - SiliconANGLE Marketing intelligence company Ahrefs Pte\. Ltd\. today launched Letaido, an agent-powered marketing workspace built to take over the recurring research, reporting and monitoring work that fills up a marketing team’s week\. In most marketing departments, generative artificial intelligence is still something people use on their own\. A writer drafts with it\. An analyst pulls numbers\. Nothing joins the two up\. The Boston Consulting Group Inc\. surveyed 300 marketing chiefs for its 2026 global CMO report and found 42% still using generative AI only on discrete tasks\. Agents running across multiple workflows showed up at 32%\. Only about 8% said they run campaigns where several agents work autonomously\. Letaido is pitched as the shared layer that has been missing\. Teams can hand agents multistep jobs, schedule recurring workflows, build dashboards and reports, and set up continuous monitoring of their own sites and their competitors\. # AI SEO monitoring platforms emerge as brands chase visibility in answers Semrush expanded its AI Visibility Index in 2026 based on 126 million real user prompts\. Brands are no longer measuring search visibility only by ranking positions\. The new gap is whether an AI system cites them, mentions them, or leaves them out of the answer altogether, and Trend Hunter recently featured AI SEO Monitoring Platforms as their own software category\. ## The measurement gap is now the product Traditional SEO tools were built for blue links, not generated answers\. In AI-driven search, a brand can be present in the response without owning a click path, or absent from the answer even when it still ranks well in classic search\. That is why monitoring platforms are moving beyond content production and into observability, analysis, and competitive intelligence\. Semrush has helped define that shift with its AI Visibility Index\. The original index launched in September 2025\. # Ahrefs study finds 67% of ChatGPT citations are off-limits to marketers Ahrefs found that 67% of ChatGPT’s top 1,000 citations are off-limits to marketers, a split that exposes how far AI answers lean beyond owned brand pages\. The study is based on the top 1,000 most-cited pages in ChatGPT, and the mix points to Wikipedia, community forums, review platforms and other third-party sources that brands can influence only indirectly\. That is the mismatch at the center of AI search visibility\. Ranking a homepage, product page or blog post still matters, but it no longer guarantees inclusion in the pages ChatGPT chooses to cite\. Ahrefs’ citation analysis shows that the most useful material for AI systems often comes from comparison pages and category roundups rather than a company’s own site\. The strongest example is the content format Ahrefs identified as dominant: 43\.8% of cited pages are “Best X” listicles\. Tim Soulo said on X that Ahrefs analyzed over 1 billion data points across 14 studies in six months and concluded that “‘Best X’ blog listicles are the single most prominent content format cited by AI chatbots\. # Heavily AI-Flagged Pages Still Rank Across Google's Top 10 AI-heavy pages turn up at every spot in Google’s top 10\. But pages the detector reads as mostly AI-written sit lower in those results than pages with little AI text, and fewer of them were found in the index at all, according to new data\. The scores come from Ahrefs’ own AI detector, which the company sells through Site Audit and Site Explorer\. It says the tool isn’t perfect and doesn’t work the same way as anything Google might use\. Every number here is an estimate of how much of a page reads as AI-written, not a record of who wrote it\. Since 2023, Google has said that it rewards quality no matter how a page was made, and that automation aimed mainly at gaming rankings counts as spam\. More than half of the pages in Google’s top three search results \(54\.7%\) have less than 20% AI-generated content\.
